guarantees.claim: All six prim_subreg_shadow instances have de tied to 0 and d tied to '0, so hardware cannot directly update these shadowed control registers; updates can only come from software writes via we_i and ctrl_wd.

The we_i input is shared among all six instances, causing all control fields (operation, mode, key_len, sideload, prng_reseed_rate, manual_operation) to be written together atomically on a single write strobe.

assumptions.claim: The external logic asserts we_i only for a full-word write to the AES control register, and ctrl_wd provides stable, correct field values at that time.
assumptions.risk: Spurious or partial we_i assertion could corrupt control values, leading to illegal AES configuration (wrong mode, key length, sideload enable) that may expose secret data or cause operational failure.

assumptions.claim: The read-enable signals reg2hw_ctrl_i.<field>.re are asserted by the register block only during valid read cycles according to the prim_subreg_shadow protocol.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect .re timing could cause shadow register state corruption or incorrect readback data, potentially leaking secret or stale values.

assumptions.claim: rst_ni and rst_shadowed_ni are asserted/deasserted properly to initialize shadow registers to their RESVAL values as defined in the instances.
assumptions.risk: If reset fails, control registers may be in unknown state, leading to unintended AES operation (e.g., enabling sideload, wrong mode) that could expose keys or cause security breach.

uncertain_points.claim: The .qe (error queue) outputs of all prim_subreg_shadow instances are left unconnected, potentially discarding fault detection information that could be used to escalate alert or latch error details.
uncertain_points.cond: when a shadow register mismatch is detected
uncertain_points.risk: If a fault injection causes a shadow mismatch, the error queue may capture critical data (e.g., which register, time) but is lost; this could reduce the system's ability to respond to or log the attack.

uncertain_points.claim: The err_update and err_storage signals from each instance are generated but not used in this chunk; their integration into a global error/alert mechanism is not visible.
uncertain_points.risk: These error signals might not be properly aggregated or might mask faults if not connected to an alert handler, allowing a shadow mismatch to go unnoticed.

uncertain_points.claim: The shared we_i assumes full-word write; if the bus interface supports sub-word writes (byte/half-word), partial field update could lead to inconsistent configuration.
uncertain_points.cond: if sub-word write operations are possible
uncertain_points.risk: Partial write to the control register might update only some fields, leaving others stale, causing mismatch between configured operation, key length, and sideload, which could open security weaknesses.

uncertain_points.claim: ctrl_wd must be stable when we_i is asserted; any race condition where ctrl_wd changes just after we_i deassertion but before the register latches could capture inconsistent data.
uncertain_points.risk: If ctrl_wd is not held, the captured control value might be corrupt, leading to wrong AES operation (e.g., incorrect mode, enabling manual operation unexpectedly).
